subject: Ridgewell private deployment preflight — ops, networking & legal gating
messages:
From: Tom Hsiao <tom@ridgewell.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@ridgewell.com
Date: Fri, 28 Jun 2029 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Ridgewell private deployment — kickoff & preflight questions

Sergio, thanks for the quick intro earlier. We chatted internally and want to start a short preflight to confirm what we need to lock down before hardware goes on-site. High level asks from Ridgewell: 

- Network egress window and allowed destinations (we operate behind strict egress proxies)
- KMS/HSM integration options and key custody model for on-prem deployment
- Data retention and snapshot lifecycle for model artifacts and logs
- Whether Redwood supports air-gapped delivery for initial image install

I attached a rough network diagram (see attachment) and our procurement point-of-contact is cc'd. Can you confirm what you need from us to complete the security questionnaire (SOC2 artifacts, encryption matrix, runbook for incident response)? Also propose a 30–45m preflight on Mon/Tue next week.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Hsiao
Head of Cloud Infrastructure
Ridgewell Systems
[attachment: ridgewell-network-diagram.pdf (pdf)]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Hsiao <tom@ridgewell.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jun 2029 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ridgewell private deployment — kickoff & preflight questions

Thanks Tom — appreciate the clear list and the diagram. Looping in Marissa (Solutions Engineering) and Neha (Security & Compliance) so we can cover both staging/install and the legal/security gating.

Quick answers / what we need from Ridgewell before we lock a date: 

- Egress: we support policy-based routing for allowed destinations and can provide a minimal allowlist for telemetry, model fetching, and license checks. If you need a fully offline install we have an "airgap bundle" process but that requires a signed runbook and onsite engineer windows.
- KMS: we support KMS/HSM integrations via PKCS#11 and an external KMS endpoint (customer-managed). We'll need certificate exchange and a test key during preflight.
- Retention: by default we keep model artifacts in the on-prem object store for 90 days; we can change policies and configure tiering to cold storage. Snapshots can be scheduled; we'll include suggested lifecycle rules in the checklist.
- Artifacts: SOC2 artifacts we can share under an NDA. Neha will own the artifact list and provide a Redacted SOC2 summary + our audit contact.

Action items I can take before the call: 
1) Send the Redwood preflight checklist (ops + security) — attachment.
2) Draft a minimal allowlist for network ops (outbound FQDNs and ports).
3) Propose two time slots: Mon 2029-07-01 09:00–09:45 PT or Tue 2029-07-02 11:00–11:45 PT.

Can Ridgewell confirm which slot works and whether you prefer video or phone-only? We'll include a runbook excerpt showing the on-prem image install steps and the KMS handshake.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
s: +1 (415) 555-0123
[attachment: ridgewell-preflight-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Tom Hsiao <tom@ridgewell.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@ridgewell.com
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2029 08:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ridgewell private deployment — kickoff & preflight questions

Sergio — thanks for the quick turnaround and the checklist. Procurement prefers Tue and video. A few clarifications before we meet: 

- Airgap: we will likely require an airgapped initial install for the first phase. Please flag the exact runbook steps we must sign off on (we need to share with our on-site ops team).
- KMS: Ridgewell uses an on-prem HSM (Thales). We'll need to validate PKCS#11 compatibility and the certificate exchange flow. Who on Redwood owns the HSM test?
- Network allowlist: the diagram is minimal; we will add our proxy egress IPs. Please be explicit about any outbound connections to redwood-managed services and whether they can be aliased to a single FQDN.
- Legal / procurement: procurement asked for a list of any third-party sub-processors used during on-prem installs and whether Redwood's on-site engineers sign a separate NDA.

Attaching a one-page list of procurement questions and the on-premops contact details.

Tom
Tom Hsiao
Head of Cloud Infrastructure
Ridgewell Systems
[attachment: procurement-questions.pdf (pdf)]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Hsiao <tom@ridgewell.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@ridgewell.com
Date: Sun, 30 Jun 2029 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ridgewell private deployment — kickoff & preflight questions

Tom — great, Tue + video it is. Couple upfront notes ahead of the meeting so your team has context (below is a short pre-read). I included answers inline to your procurement points and flagged who will own each item.

- Airgap install: we maintain an airgap image bundle and a signed install runbook. Operationally this means: checksum-verified ISO, offline license token exchange over an SFTP handoff, and a one-window remote session for bootstrap validation. Marissa will present the install steps and handoff responsibilities. (Owner: Marissa Cole)

- HSM/KMS: Redwood supports PKCS#11 and a Thales HSM is on our compatibility list. We'll need a test key and a temporary test user account to validate the sign/unwrap flow. Neha will own the security test and can run a lab validation ahead of the on-site install if you can share a test endpoint. (Owner: Neha Kapoor)

- Outbound connections / allowlist: minimal behavior: license check, optional telemetry (configurable), and model fetches (one FQDN per model repository). We can produce a single DNS alias for the model repo traffic and provide IP ranges if you prefer a CIDR block. (Owner: Sergio)

- Third-party subprocessors & NDAs: Redwood's on-site engineers are Redwood employees and operate under our standard employee NDA and background checks for customer on-site work. For airgapped installs we can sign a supplemental SOW clause and limited on-site NDA per your legal team. (Owner: Legal / Partnerships — I'll surface this in the call.)

Preflight deliverables attached: 
- Ridgewell preflight checklist (our version) — covers ops, storage lifecycle, and node ring sizing guidelines.
- Short runbook excerpt for airgap bundle and KMS handshake.

Please confirm the video link you prefer — we'll send a calendar invite for Tue 2029-07-02 11:00 PT and include a recording permission flag for compliance. Looking forward to the call.
